summary.short: Sets horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements placed on the EU market, imposing duties on manufacturers and other economic operators covering design, vulnerability handling, support periods of at least five years and incident reporting. Reporting duties apply from 11 September 2026.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act) sets horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements (software or hardware, with remote data processing) made available on the Union market. Excluded are products under Regulations 2017/745, 2017/746 and 2019/2144, and national security products (Art. 2). Products must meet the essential requirements in Annex I, and manufacturers' vulnerability processes must comply (Art. 6). Manufacturers must assess and document cybersecurity risks, set a support period of at least five years or the expected use time, provide security updates, designate a single point of contact and exercise due diligence on third-party components (Art. 13). They must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents to a CSIRT and ENISA via a single reporting platform, with a 24-hour early warning and a 72-hour notification (Art. 14). Important products (classes I and II, Art. 7) and critical products (Art. 8) face conformity assessment, with third-party assessment for class II. Recitals give application from 11 December 2027. The text provided is part 1 of 2; enforcement and market surveillance provisions are not included.

notes: Part 1 of 2: covers the preamble (recitals 1 to 130) and Articles 1 to 15 only; the Annexes, Articles 16 onward and any amending provisions are in part 2 and not annotated here. Application dates (11 Jun 2026 for notified body provisions, 11 Sep 2026 for reporting obligations, 11 Dec 2027 general) appear in this part only in recital 126; the operative application provision is in part 2. Several operative provisions refer to provisions in part 2 (Articles 16, 32, 52, 61, 62 and Annexes I to VII), e.g. Art. 7(1), 8(1), 12(3), 13(8), 13(25), 14(1) to 14(10). Recital-only references (e.g. Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Directive (EU) 2024/2853, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482, Recommendation (EU) 2019/534) are not coded as relations. Internal tension for readers: the severity test in Art. 14(5)(a) refers to sensitive or important data or functions, whereas the incident definition in Art. 3(44) refers to availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of data or functions; both are coded as written. Art. 14(2)(c) (final report within 14 days after a corrective measure is available) and Art. 14(4)(c) (final report within one month after the incident notification) concern different notification types and are not in conflict. Part 2 of 2 covers Articles 16 to 71 and Annexes I to VIII. Only relations, entities and notes are annotated here. No registry IDs were supplied, so target_instrument_id is an empty string and targets are identified in target_text. Article 71(2) applies Article 14 from 11 September 2026 and Chapter IV from 11 June 2026, while general application is 11 December 2027 (Art 71(2), Art 69(2)-(3)). Article 33(1) refers to microenterprises and small enterprises, while Art 33(3) and other provisions refer to microenterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises. ‘product with digital elements’ means a software or hardware product and its remote data processing solutions, including software or hardware components being placed on the market separately;
‘remote data processing’ means data processing at a distance for which the software is designed and developed by the manufacturer, or under the responsibility of the manufacturer
‘electronic information system’ means a system, including electrical or electronic equipment, capable of processing, storing or transmitting digital data;
‘software’ means the part of an electronic information system which consists of computer code;
‘hardware’ means a physical electronic information system, or parts thereof capable of processing, storing or transmitting digital data;
‘component’ means software or hardware intended for integration into an electronic information system;
